issues.description: Class name and constructor/destructor identifiers are inconsistent in the Bitmap24 header: the header declares 'class Image24' while the constructors/destructor are named 'Bitmap24' (and implemented as Bitmap24::... in the .cpp). This mismatch will cause compilation errors and prevents students from building or running the example and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name and its constructors/destructor consistent. The simplest fix is to rename 'class Image24' in Bitmap24.hpp to 'class Bitmap24' (so constructor/destructor names match), or alternatively rename the constructor/destructor declarations to 'Image24' and update the .cpp accordingly. Ensure header guard and filenames remain consistent with the chosen class name.

issues.description: The template repository header example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares the image class as 'Image24', while the implementation example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp (template) and the solution header/implementation use the class name 'Bitmap24'. This mismatch between the declared class name in the template header and the class name used in the implementation/solution creates confusion for students: they cannot reliably map the header declaration to the implementation, will encounter build errors or symbol mismatches, and may waste time tracing whether to follow the template or the solution naming.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template repository, rename the class declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'class Image24' to 'class Bitmap24' (and adjust any constructor/destructor declarations accordingly) so that the header matches the implementation in example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp and aligns with the solution naming.
